explain: Read the evict cycle in order. 1. evict clears valid and dirty for line 0. 2. countWb then finds the line neither valid nor dirty, so its guard is false. This happens in every evict, so writebacks stays 0 for the whole run, although io_writeback is high at cycles 2 and 4. (The read at cycle 5 and the later evict of a clean line do not change it either.) countWb's guard held at the start of the cycle but not where the rule runs: the Simulation pane marks it blocked.

explain: Now the cycle goes: 1. write and readMiss do nothing in an evict cycle. 2. countWb runs before evict: the line is still valid and dirty, so writebacks goes up by one. 3. evict clears the line. The dirty eviction at cycle 2 shows as writebacks = 1 at cycle 3, and the one at cycle 4 as 2 at cycle 5. You can also add writebacks <= dirty[req_line] ? writebacks + 1 : writebacks; to evict and drop countWb.
